title: Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance

tasks.short: Assign crews, equipment and vehicles to jobs, then transmit assignments and confirm receipt.

steps.what: Read the work order, location, timing and service requirements.
Check crew availability, qualifications and equipment against the dispatch requirements.
Confirm uncertain availability, access and practical constraints by telephone or radio.
Compare feasible assignments on the dispatch board.
Choose the assignment and authorize its release.
Transmit the approved assignment to the crew by telephone or radio.
Acknowledge receipt of the assignment.

tasks.design: Connect work orders and resource status in the {OPS_SYSTEM} to relevant availability and qualification records in the {HCM}. A deterministic solver on the {DATA_PLATFORM} proposes feasible assignments; the dispatcher authorizes release, and the {WORKFLOW} sends instructions and tracks acknowledgements. Telephone and radio remain available for unclear constraints, critical instructions and connectivity failures.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability went stale between systems and field calls. Dispatch rules included undocumented local knowledge, making reliable live replanning expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured resource feeds and established constraint solvers can support live proposals. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and checks; field judgement still needs people.
tasks.still_hard: Travel times, equipment condition and practical access can change without a system event. GDPR applies to worker data; national rules may require consultation, and EU AI Act classification needs assessment if allocation uses personal traits or behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher weighs urgency, crew fatigue and local conditions, then takes responsibility for a workable assignment.

ambition.what: Reconsider the next two hours of assignments whenever a delay threatens a service commitment.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time checking screens and repeating instructions, and more time resolving competing priorities. Existing dispatch authority stays with the dispatcher; broader spending or staffing rights require separate delegation.

reach.task: Compare recovery options when delays threaten delivery commitments.
reach.learn: Constraint modelling, travel-time uncertainty and the operational cost of reassignment.

reach.task: Prioritize urgent field repairs across sites.
reach.learn: Asset criticality, site access restrictions and service restoration priorities.

evidence.claim: Boltrics 3PL Dynamics provides transport and operational records; this supports the records foundation, not a proven live dispatch solver.
Constraint solvers can propose assignments from explicit availability, qualification, timing and equipment rules.
Worker-data processing requires GDPR safeguards; applicable national consultation rules and EU AI Act classification need assessment.

assumptions: The company has a dispatch board in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; telephone and radio handle field exceptions.
Jobs have structured locations, service windows and basic resource requirements.
Routine instructions can move to an accessible field interface; acknowledgement still requires the recipient.
The proposed solver uses operational constraints rather than inferred worker behaviour.
Time shares are estimates across actors; these tasks overlap and their savings should not be added.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a limited rollout. Consultation and access waiting can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which planning and notification features are already licensed in the {OPS_SYSTEM}?
How current are crew availability, qualification and equipment records?
Which crews have reliable field connectivity?
Which assignments require supervisor approval or critical read-back?
Which national employment and consultation rules apply?
What time shares and exception rates appear in actual dispatch logs?
research_questions: Which solver approach gives useful alternatives within the required dispatch response time?
How should stale resource feeds suppress proposals without blocking unrelated jobs?
Which field acknowledgement patterns work during intermittent connectivity?
new_work: Review infeasible jobs and stale resource warnings.
Maintain qualification, timing, travel and equipment constraints.
Handle failed notifications and missing acknowledgements.
Check reassignment outcomes for avoidable disruption.
Maintain access controls, integrations and worker-data retention.
tasks.statement: Schedule or dispatch workers, work crews, equipment, or service vehicles to appropriate locations, according to customer requests, specifications, or needs, using radios or telephones.

tasks.short: Coordinate repairs and recovery plans when vehicles or equipment interrupt scheduled service.

steps.what: Receive the breakdown call and establish immediate service and safety implications.
Check equipment history, warranty, assigned jobs and available replacement resources.
Call maintenance providers to establish repair availability, likely delays and alternatives.
Choose repair or replacement by comparing downtime, service commitments and cost.
Approve exceptional spending or service trade-offs beyond the dispatcher's delegated limits.
Book the selected repair and communicate equipment location and access details.
Revise affected jobs and resource assignments around the expected repair window.
Confirm technical clearance before returning repaired equipment to service.

tasks.design: Configured views in {OPS_SYSTEM} assemble the incident, equipment history and affected jobs; deterministic comparisons show recovery options and feasible schedule revisions. A flow in {WORKFLOW} prepares repair instructions for approval and sends them through {EMAIL}, while provider negotiation, exceptional spending and technical clearance remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair coordination combines incomplete fault information, uncertain provider availability and service trade-offs across separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can feed a reusable recovery brief, while inexpensive deterministic code compares scenarios and prepares the paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Diagnosis, uncertain repair times, supplier commitments and competing customer consequences remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Securing a credible repair commitment and choosing which disruption the operation can tolerate.

ambition.what: An incident recovery brief comparing repair and replacement before a booking decision.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends more time negotiating recovery and less time assembling histories or rewriting schedules. They gain clearer choices within existing delegated limits; exceptional spending and technical clearance keep their current approvers.

reach.task: Define fallback resources for the loss of a critical vehicle or equipment type.
reach.learn: Recovery priorities, dependency mapping and minimum service levels.

evidence.claim: Deterministic constraint checks can compare recovery schedules, but repair uncertainty still requires human judgement.
Operational systems offer an existing base for transport and resource records; this does not prove repair coordination automation.
A vendor case documents benefits from appointment scheduling in freight operations, an adjacent rather than equivalent use.

assumptions: The scope is coordination and administration; physical diagnosis and repair are excluded.
Provider negotiation remains a conversation, so no model loop is required.
Exceptional approval is conditional; its share represents average effort across repair incidents.
Routine plans within delegated limits bypass exceptional spending approval.
Schedule revisions enter the normal dispatch release process before crews act.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates.
GDPR and applicable national rules govern personal data and changed working arrangements.
unknowns: Actual spending limits and escalation responsibilities.
Availability and quality of equipment history and replacement-resource records.
Provider booking channels, cancellation terms and access requirements.
Who is authorised to certify equipment for return to service.
Applicable employee consultation requirements for schedule changes.
research_questions: Which recovery choices can be compared using reliable cost and downtime inputs?
Can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} views assemble the recovery brief?
How should the system handle uncertain repair estimates without creating false commitments?
new_work: Maintain provider contacts, spending limits and fallback-resource rules.
Resolve failed bookings and changes to repair estimates.
Check that schedule revisions reach the normal release queue.
Record technical clearance and review unresolved incidents.
tasks.statement: Arrange for necessary repairs to restore service and schedules.

tasks.short: Relay field instructions and messages, confirm understanding and keep a transmission record.

steps.what: Receive a field message by telephone or two-way radio.
Match the message to the job and check the latest instruction.
Clarify unclear details or conflicting instructions with the sender.
Select the recipient and authorize the instruction to be relayed.
Relay the instruction to the crew, supervisor or field inspector.
Acknowledge receipt and read back critical instructions.
Copy transmission details and acknowledgement into the job record.

tasks.design: Configure job-linked messages and acknowledgements in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with the {WORKFLOW} routing dispatcher-approved instructions to the current recipient. Delivery events create the transmission log automatically, removing separate copying; telephone and radio remain for ambiguity, critical read-back and failed digital delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Voice channels did not share job identifiers, recipient lists or delivery events with the operational record. Repeating and logging messages was the reliable bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured message forms, job-linked field interfaces and delivery events can remove routine repetition. Deterministic routing uses the current crew assignment without interpreting free text.
tasks.still_hard: A delivery receipt proves receipt, not understanding. Radio-only crews, noisy environments and changed instructions still require conversation; GDPR, applicable EU AI Act duties and national rules govern any new worker logging or monitoring.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher notices ambiguity and conflicting instructions. The field worker confirms what can actually be understood and carried out safely.
tasks.altitude: The dispatcher repeats fewer routine messages and spends less time copying logs, leaving more attention for unclear or urgent instructions. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Design a communication fallback when field connectivity fails.
reach.learn: Channel failure modes, escalation timing and acknowledgement procedures.

reach.task: Verify that operational instructions are received and understood.
reach.learn: Instruction version control, evidence of receipt and critical read-back.

evidence.claim: TransFollow and Qargo support creating and signing digital consignment notes within the transport system; this supports shared instruction records, not radio replacement.
Job-linked notifications, recipient routing and delivery logs can use deterministic workflow rules.
Critical read-back remains a human communication control; a technical delivery receipt does not establish understanding.

assumptions: The {OPS_SYSTEM} maintains current job-to-crew assignments.
Routine messages can use structured fields and a digital field interface.
A telephone or radio fallback remains available.
Clarification time is concentrated in exceptional messages, so automation leaves that step intact.
Automatic logs capture digital events; fallback voice messages still need a short exception entry.
The target does not classify call content or score worker performance.
Build ranges cover one operating team and applicable access and employee consultation work.

How accurately does the dispatch board identify current recipients?
Which instructions require read-back?
How often do radio-only or offline situations occur?
Can the existing {OPS_SYSTEM} capture delivery and acknowledgement events?
Which national consultation and retention requirements apply to transmission logs?
research_questions: Which acknowledgement design avoids confusing receipt with operational acceptance?
How should revised instructions supersede earlier messages on an offline device?
What escalation timing works for missed acknowledgements without creating notification overload?
new_work: Handle failed deliveries and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain recipient routing and escalation rules.
Record short exception logs for voice-only communication.
Check that revised instructions supersede earlier versions.
Maintain devices, access rights, log retention and communication fallback procedures.
tasks.statement: Relay work orders, messages, or information to or from work crews, supervisors, or field inspectors, using telephones or two-way radios.

tasks.short: Discuss service questions and problems, agree workable options and record the resulting actions.

steps.what: Hear the customer's or supervisor's question and establish the requested outcome.
Check job status, service terms and available options.
Approve a proposed service exception beyond the dispatcher's delegated limits.
Explain feasible options and agree the next action.
Record the agreement and update the work order when service changes.

loop.input: Dispatcher's agreement notes, current work order and allowed update fields.
loop.output: Proposed case summary and work-order field changes with supporting note excerpts.
loop.check: Validate identifiers, dates and allowed fields; the dispatcher confirms commitments before saving.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per case; missing or conflicting commitments go to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Agreement notes use varied language. Structured forms remain the cheaper option where accepted.

tasks.design: A deterministic case view joins status and capacity from the {OPS_SYSTEM} with approved service terms from the {DOCS}. The dispatcher conducts the conversation, obtains approval only for exceptions beyond delegated limits, and reviews a bounded extraction of agreement notes before the {WORKFLOW} saves changes in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The answer depended on scattered status, service terms and supervisor knowledge. Informal agreements then needed manual transcription into operational records.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared identifiers and rule-based lookups can bring the relevant facts into one view. Bounded extraction can turn short notes into proposed updates with a clear review point.
tasks.still_hard: The system cannot settle disputed expectations or promise capacity that has not been confirmed. GDPR governs notes and access; EU AI Act duties depend on the deployed features, and new employee monitoring may trigger national consultation rules.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher listens for the real problem, explains trade-offs and rebuilds trust when service has failed.

ambition.what: Offer a feasible revised service slot during the first customer call.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time searching and writing up calls, leaving more time for difficult agreements. The software grants no new authority to waive charges, add resources or change contractual commitments.

reach.task: Agree service changes without losing track of scope and dependencies.
reach.learn: Change acceptance, dependency checks and explicit ownership of the next action.
Service recovery, delegated spending limits and clear escalation criteria.

evidence.claim: Structured status and policy lookups can prepare a service conversation without automating the negotiation.
A bounded extraction loop can propose record changes from free-text notes, with schema checks and human confirmation.
The digest provides no documented case establishing savings for this specific customer-conversation task.

assumptions: Telephone calls are common; some inquiries also arrive through the {EMAIL}.
Service terms and delegation limits can be represented as approved structured fields.
Supervisor approval is conditional; its time share is an average across routine and exceptional inquiries.
The loop receives dispatcher notes and does not require recording calls.
A structured entry form replaces the loop if dispatchers find it easier.
Build ranges cover one service queue, relevant access and consultation where applicable.

How often do calls involve disputed commitments or supervisor approval?
What personal information appears in service notes?
Does the company already have an approved note-entry workflow?
research_questions: Does a structured agreement form outperform note extraction for typical calls?
Which source checks best detect invented or altered service commitments?
How should the case view display stale capacity and uncertain completion times?
new_work: Review extracted commitments before saving.
Correct incomplete notes and handle conflicting dates or instructions.
Maintain service terms and delegation limits.
Audit a sample of record changes for unsupported commitments.
Maintain the extraction schema, prompts, access and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Confer with customers or supervising personnel to address questions, problems, or requests for service or equipment.

tasks.short: Prepare daily crew and vehicle run schedules, resolve conflicts and publish the approved plan.

steps.what: Retrieve due jobs and service windows.
Check the crew roster, absences, qualifications and equipment availability.
Resolve missing durations, access restrictions and capacity assumptions with the operations supervisor.
Sequence jobs and assign resources in the schedule workbook.
Review conflicts and approve the daily run schedule.
Format and issue crew run sheets from the approved schedule.

tasks.design: Configure daily planning in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with availability and qualification feeds from the {HCM} and deterministic checks for overlaps, working time and equipment conflicts. The operations supervisor approves the proposed schedule before the {WORKFLOW} issues crew run sheets and stores the approved version in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The schedule workbook joined job demand to staffing and equipment data that changed separately. Planning features existed, but integration and rule setup were costly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling modules and structured exports can replace much of the workbook assembly. Faster adapter development makes a limited, rules-based rollout more affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Real job durations, access constraints and staffing compromises remain uncertain. GDPR, applicable EU AI Act duties and national rules on working-time changes or employee consultation must be assessed before rollout.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor understands which service commitments can move and when a mathematically feasible schedule would overload a crew.

ambition.what: Choose the next day's reserve capacity before accepting late service requests.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less of the week assembling schedules and can compare capacity scenarios with the supervisor. Schedule approval and staffing decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile daily workload with constrained resource capacity.
reach.learn: Capacity buffers, duration estimates and the difference between hard constraints and preferences.

reach.task: Set reserve capacity for expected demand peaks.
reach.learn: Demand uncertainty, service-level trade-offs and the cost of unused capacity.

evidence.claim: Configurable planning modules can assemble schedules from structured demand, resource calendars and explicit constraints.
The Smurfit Kappa Hoya case documents loading-bay time-slot scheduling; it does not establish the same gains for crew scheduling.
Worker scheduling and associated personal-data processing require assessment under GDPR, the EU AI Act and applicable national rules.

assumptions: The {OPS_SYSTEM} holds jobs, while a {SPREADSHEET} joins the daily plan across teams.
A configurable planning module can represent the ordinary run templates and constraints.
If that module is unavailable, a deterministic scheduling component is needed and the build estimate increases.
Scheduling receives availability flags rather than medical reasons for absence.
The operations supervisor currently approves the daily schedule.
Build ranges include a limited pilot, access setup and applicable consultation effort; elapsed approval time can be longer.

Which working-time agreements and national consultation rules apply?
How accurate are planned job durations?
How many schedule revisions occur each day?
Are machine-readable crew and equipment calendars available?
research_questions: Which schedule checks can be configured in existing modules without custom code?
How should the planner represent duration uncertainty and reserve capacity?
Which measures reveal whether a schedule is practical during a pilot?
new_work: Review schedule conflicts and capacity warnings.
Maintain calendars, run templates and constraint settings.
Compare planned durations with actual completion times.
Investigate stale availability feeds and failed schedule publication.
Review access, retention and scheduling-rule changes with the relevant employee representatives.
tasks.statement: Prepare daily work and run schedules.

tasks.short: Receive service requests, clarify requirements and prepare work orders for dispatch.

steps.what: Read emailed service requests and identify the requested work.

loop.output: Request fields with source passages and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate required fields, formats and source support; flag conflicting instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per request; send unresolved fields to the dispatcher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests describe locations, faults and access instructions in varied free text.

steps.what: Check customer, site and equipment details against existing records.
Call the requester to resolve missing details, urgency and access arrangements.
Determine service scope, priority and required skills or equipment.
Enter the work order using the agreed service requirements.
Check the completed order and release it to the dispatch queue.

tasks.design: A reusable intake template in {WORKFLOW} receives requests from {EMAIL}; a bounded extraction loop proposes fields and deterministic checks match records in {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Configured forms generate the draft work order, while the dispatcher resolves ambiguity and approves release to the dispatch queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Request formats vary, reference records disagree and connecting the mailbox to operational records took bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and interfaces handle structured requests; bounded extraction handles variable text, and AI-assisted coding reduces adapter development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous urgency, incomplete site information and unreliable reference records still require operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a routine request conceals a dangerous fault, unrealistic promise or sensitive customer situation.

ambition.what: A request-readiness check that identifies missing access details before scheduling.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time copying requests and more time resolving unclear work before it reaches crews. They can return incomplete requests for clarification; spending and service-promise authority do not automatically expand.

reach.task: Check whether incoming work is sufficiently defined for scheduling.
reach.learn: Scope boundaries, acceptance criteria and dependency checks.

evidence.claim: PDF order extraction is an existing capability; applying it to service requests needs local validation.
Integrated operational systems already maintain transport and warehouse records.
Deterministic matching, required-field checks and work-order templates can handle structured intake.

assumptions: The baseline is a mobile service operation within a company of 200 to 2,000 staff.
Some requests arrive through email, while operational records already reside in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The reusable intake schema can be prepared independently; live processing requires authorised company access.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the implemented use.
unknowns: Actual request channels, volumes and attachment formats.
Available interfaces and customer or equipment identifiers.
Local priority rules and who may release work orders.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which existing {OPS_SYSTEM} intake features cover the required fields?
Which request ambiguities cause the most dispatch rework?
Can extraction preserve every safety-relevant instruction in a representative sample?
new_work: Review extracted fields and resolve unmatched records.
Maintain intake schemas, validation rules and connector mappings.
Sample released orders for omitted instructions and incorrect priorities.
Maintain access controls and request-data retention.

tasks.short: Coordinate communications and resolve dispatch issues across an assigned territory.

steps.what: Monitor incoming calls, messages and job updates for the assigned territory.
Set priorities and decide who should handle each issue.
Clarify conflicting reports and coordinate responses with crews and supervisors.
Relay agreed updates to responsible teams and track outstanding replies.
Copy communication times, owners and reply status into the handover log.

tasks.design: An integration brings communication metadata and job events from the {TELEPHONY}, {CHAT} and {OPS_SYSTEM} into a territory queue. Configured ownership and escalation rules suggest routing; the dispatcher settles priorities and handles ambiguous conversations through the {TELEPHONY} or {OTHER} radio system. Agreed updates trigger notifications, and the shared queue replaces the copied handover log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Territory ownership, job identifiers and acknowledgement status are spread across channels. A copied log compensates for missing links between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Event interfaces and configurable queues can connect communication metadata to job records. Deterministic routing covers known territories and message types without interpreting every conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Unidentified callers, conflicting accounts and simultaneous incidents still need attention. Recording or analysing staff communications adds GDPR obligations and may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher recognises when an apparently routine update signals a larger problem and negotiates priorities between teams.

ambition.what: Territory backlog balancing at each shift handover.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time finding messages and chasing routine replies. More time goes to unresolved conflicts and shift preparation; cross-territory staffing changes still require supervisor approval.

reach.task: Identify recurring delays between dispatch and field teams.
reach.learn: Queue analysis, process mapping and separating workload effects from individual performance.

evidence.claim: Known job identifiers, territories and message types support deterministic queue routing and reminders.
A shared event history can replace duplicate transcription of communication metadata.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent can apply to systems monitoring employee activity.

assumptions: The company has defined territories, escalation paths and shift handovers.
The OTHER system is a radio system.
Routing uses explicit identifiers and declared message types; unknown messages remain for human triage.
The target stores necessary metadata and agreed responses without adding call transcription.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates.
unknowns: Which communication channels expose supported event interfaces.
How reliably calls and messages can be linked to jobs.
Existing retention periods and employee consultation arrangements.

Which reminder rules reduce missed replies without creating notification overload?
Can existing queue configuration eliminate the handover spreadsheet?

Resolve unidentified messages and broken job links.
Monitor missed events, duplicate notifications and overdue acknowledgements.
Review access permissions and communication-metadata retention.
tasks.statement: Oversee all communications within specifically assigned territories.

tasks.short: Track crew and equipment availability, identify service risks and coordinate schedule changes.

steps.what: Inspect location and job-status screens for crew availability, delays and idle equipment.
Contact crews when location or availability is missing, stale or inconsistent.
Calculate busy time, waiting time and available capacity in the shift workbook.
Compare open jobs with available crews, equipment, qualifications and remaining working time.
Choose reassignments after considering service urgency, crew context and customer commitments.
Transmit changed assignments and practical instructions to the affected crews.
Acknowledge the assignment or report a practical obstacle.

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to show fresh resource status and acknowledge assignments; deterministic jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} calculate utilisation and feasible schedule candidates using authorised roster data from {HCM}. The dispatcher approves reassignments and instruction release, while stale data, infeasible jobs and missing acknowledgements enter an exception queue in {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Location feeds, crew updates and rosters were disconnected, while scheduling rules were held in dispatchers' experience.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing event feeds, configurable alerts and deterministic solvers can be joined more cheaply with AI-assisted coding; no autonomous agent is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Stale signals, uncertain job duration and unrecorded crew constraints can make a mathematically feasible schedule impractical.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a crew appears idle and balancing customer urgency with safe, workable assignments.

ambition.what: Reassess threatened service windows whenever a material delay or equipment outage occurs.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher moves from repeatedly scanning screens to reviewing a ranked exception queue and feasible alternatives. They can propose earlier recovery within existing dispatch authority; employment and disciplinary decisions remain outside this tool.

reach.task: Identify recurring capacity bottlenecks by time window and resource type.
reach.learn: Event-data quality, queue measures and the difference between utilisation and service performance.

evidence.claim: Operational transport systems provide an existing foundation for dispatch records and resource coordination.
A documented vendor case reports reduced truck turnaround through appointment scheduling; it does not validate workforce tracking.
AI used for certain worker allocation, monitoring or evaluation purposes can fall within Annex III employment provisions.
In the Netherlands, working-time arrangements and certain employee monitoring systems involve works-council consent provisions.
Freshness checks, utilisation calculations and constraint-based schedule candidates can use deterministic technology.

assumptions: Operational location or check-in data already exists; new tracking hardware is outside these build estimates.
The baseline includes a supplementary capacity workbook, not spreadsheet-based dispatch throughout.
The scheduler uses explicit operational constraints rather than inferred personality or behavioural scores.
Qualification and availability data is limited to what dispatch genuinely needs.
GDPR applies to identifiable location and activity data; employee agreement alone is not assumed to establish a lawful basis.
National consultation and employment rules vary; EU AI Act classification depends on the final system and purpose.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; the final acknowledgement step includes adjacent worker effort.
Consultation and access ranges are provisional and can extend the rollout calendar.

Whether off-duty tracking can be disabled.
Actual working-time, break, qualification and assignment constraints.
Available mobile acknowledgement features and roster interfaces.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
Current delegated reassignment authority.

How often do stale events create false capacity signals?

Maintain qualifications, working-time constraints and alert thresholds.
Monitor connector reliability and suppress duplicate alerts.

tasks.statement: Monitor personnel or equipment locations and utilization to coordinate service and schedules.

tasks.short: Maintain dispatch records for requests, completed work, charges, expenses and inventory movements.

steps.what: Record crew updates, work completion and service details against the work order.
Transfer charge, expense and parts details into the relevant financial records.
Compare entries with supporting records and investigate missing or conflicting details.
Approve operational corrections and release charge details for finance processing.
File supporting documents and link them to the dispatch record.
Copy dispatch totals into the shared shift summary.

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to capture structured service events once, link evidence in {DOCS} and transfer validated charge and inventory details to {ERP}. Deterministic reconciliation sends discrepancies to an approval queue, while a saved operational view replaces the duplicate shift workbook in {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work-order identifiers, financial codes and supporting documents were disconnected, making manual copying the practical bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured event capture and deterministic adapters can reuse existing records; AI-assisted coding makes company-specific mappings cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Late crew updates, disputed charges, accounting cut-offs and incorrect parts usage still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a missing update from a disputed service outcome and deciding which evidence supports a correction.

ambition.what: Review unresolved charge exceptions each shift instead of waiting for billing preparation.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher becomes an exception investigator rather than a duplicate record keeper. They gain visibility of unresolved charge evidence; finance retains accounting and invoice approval rights.

reach.task: Reconcile parts issued, used and returned against a service job.
reach.learn: Inventory transaction types, units of measure and correction controls.

evidence.claim: Operational transport systems already combine multiple categories of logistics records.
Integrated creation and signing of transport documents demonstrates linked operational evidence.
A vendor customer case reports reduced invoicing administration; it does not establish dispatcher-specific savings.
Identifier-based reconciliation and duplicate prevention need deterministic rules rather than a model.

assumptions: Crews can supply structured completion, parts and expense events; missing events remain exceptions.
Supporting documents can be linked using a work-order identifier without interpreting their free text.
The shift workbook duplicates information available from operational records.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates; no crew work is assumed to disappear.
GDPR requires appropriate access and retention; employee logging may require consultation under national rules.

Whether crew event capture is already available and used reliably.
Financial posting permissions, approval limits and retention requirements.
Whether the shift summary contains unique information that must be retained.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements.

tasks.statement: Record and maintain files or records of customer requests, work or services performed, charges, expenses, inventory, or other dispatch information.

tasks.short: Determine the people, vehicles, equipment and materials needed for work orders.

steps.what: Read work orders and identify resource requirements.

loop.output: Resource requirements with source passages and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate units, required fields and equipment codes; dispatcher accepts extracted requirements.
loop.stop: At most two extraction attempts per order; unresolved fields go to the dispatcher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable document layouts and free-text specifications resist fixed field mapping. Structured orders bypass the loop.

steps.what: Check available people, qualifications, vehicles, equipment and stock.
Calculate quantities and compare feasible resource combinations.
Clarify unusual site conditions and shortages with the field supervisor.
Select resources and record the approved resource plan.

tasks.design: A bounded extractor turns documents in the {DOCS} into draft requirements, while structured work orders bypass extraction. An integration reads availability and qualifications from the {OPS_SYSTEM}, {HCM} and {LMS}; deterministic capacity rules produce feasible options. The dispatcher confirms unusual constraints and approves the resource plan in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements, availability and qualifications sit in separate records. Local capacity rules and undocumented site constraints make a reliable match expensive to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning features, standard interfaces and faster development reduce the cost of connecting records. Bounded extraction can handle document variation without choosing assignments.
tasks.still_hard: Stale availability, missing site information and competing urgent jobs remain difficult. Staff scheduling changes require GDPR assessment and consultation under applicable national rules; EU AI Act requirements depend on the actual use.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher understands whether a technically feasible combination will work at the site and resolves competing operational priorities.

ambition.what: Resource shortage review before each dispatch wave.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into reading specifications and comparing capacity. The dispatcher retains resource approval and can bring quantified shortage options to the operations manager; no new spending rights are assumed.

reach.task: Forecast capacity shortages for the following week.
reach.learn: Capacity modelling, qualification constraints and forecast error analysis.

evidence.claim: Reading order documents into structured fields is an existing capability; this supports extraction, not resource selection.
Explicit capacity and qualification constraints can generate resource options with deterministic code.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent can apply to working-time arrangements and employee monitoring systems.

assumptions: The company handles recurring field-service or transport work with documented capacity limits.
The dispatcher normally selects resources within an existing delegation.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.
The design uses operational requirements and qualifications rather than behavioural scoring.
unknowns: Availability of supported interfaces and reliable qualification records.
Which resource constraints are documented and who can approve exceptions.
Whether the existing planning module can replace custom calculation code.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: What proportion of orders already contains structured resource requirements?
Can existing planning configuration satisfy the required constraints?
How often does a feasible plan fail because site information was missing?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve missing fields.
Maintain capacity rules, qualification mappings and equipment codes.
Investigate stale availability and infeasible plans.
Maintain interface access and test rule changes before rollout.
tasks.statement: Determine types or amounts of equipment, vehicles, materials, or personnel required, according to work orders or specifications.

tasks.short: Warn field personnel about traffic, weather and other route hazards.

steps.what: Check traffic, weather and incident information against active routes.
Confirm reported hazards and local conditions with field personnel.
Decide which crews need warnings and whether routes require changes.
Explain the warning and agree immediate action with affected personnel.
Record warnings, acknowledgements and route changes in the dispatch log.

tasks.design: An integration matches structured traffic and weather feeds from the {OTHER} traffic and weather service to active routes in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Deterministic rules flag affected crews and draft advisories; the dispatcher checks uncertain conditions and gives urgent advice through the {TELEPHONY} or {OTHER} radio system. A short form in the {OPS_SYSTEM} records the agreed action and acknowledgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Traffic information and dispatch routes are viewed separately. Reliable route matching needs current positions, consistent locations and rules for vehicle restrictions.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured feeds and route interfaces allow deterministic matching. Faster integration development makes a focused advisory screen affordable without automating live safety conversations.
tasks.still_hard: Feed delays, road conditions and safe stopping opportunities require local judgement. Drivers must receive advice without distraction, and location data needs GDPR controls.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher can clarify ambiguous hazards, check understanding and agree safe action under pressure.

ambition.what: Pre-shift route hazard brief for field crews.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time scanning maps and more time confirming consequential hazards. Advice and route decisions remain within existing authority; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Prepare diversion and service-continuity plans for severe weather.
reach.learn: Disruption scenarios, escalation thresholds and alternative service arrangements.

evidence.claim: Structured hazard locations can be matched to routes using deterministic geographic rules.
A route match does not establish that a diversion is safe for a particular vehicle or situation.
GDPR applies when route and location records identify workers.

assumptions: The company has active route records and access to a licensed structured traffic and weather service.
The OTHER systems are a traffic and weather service and a radio system.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates.
Urgent warnings remain live human communications.
unknowns: Feed coverage, update frequency, licensing and geographic accuracy.
Whether routes and vehicle restrictions are available through supported interfaces.
Existing rules for contacting moving crews and recording acknowledgements.
Whether worker consultation is required under applicable national rules.
research_questions: How frequently do stale feeds or incorrect route matches produce false alerts?
Which hazard categories can use standard advisory templates?
Can acknowledgements be captured safely through the existing field interface?
new_work: Monitor feed freshness and route-matching failures.
Maintain hazard thresholds and vehicle restriction rules.
Review false alerts and missed hazards.
Check acknowledgement records and apply location-data retention rules.
tasks.statement: Advise personnel about traffic problems, such as construction areas, accidents, congestion, weather conditions, or other hazards.

tasks.short: Order supplies and equipment, then issue them to personnel.

steps.what: Receive and clarify requests for supplies or equipment.
Check stock, reservations and usable equipment before buying.
Prepare a purchase requisition using approved suppliers and catalogue prices.
Approve the proposed supplier, quantities, price and budget allocation.
Create and send the purchase order to the supplier.
Check condition and physically hand supplies or equipment to personnel.
Record quantities, serial numbers, recipients and expected returns.

tasks.design: A catalogue request form in the {PROCUREMENT} checks stock and reservations in the {OPS_SYSTEM} before preparing a requisition. Existing approval rules route spending to the budget holder, then release a purchase order only within the approved supplier, quantity and price. Stores staff hand over items and use scanning in the {OPS_SYSTEM} to capture issue and return records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrive informally, stock records lag physical movements, and purchasing is disconnected from equipment custody. Most of the required automation already exists but needs consistent catalogues and configuration.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured request forms, approval flows and scanning remove repeated entry. Faster integration development makes the stock-to-purchasing link cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Physical condition checks, missing equipment and suitable substitutions remain human work. Automated purchasing depends on trustworthy stock and enforceable approval limits.
tasks.human_edge: People judge equipment condition, suitability and urgent substitutions, and remain accountable for physical custody.

ambition.what: Pre-booked equipment kits for scheduled field jobs.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time entering requisitions and chasing routine orders. Stores staff spend more time preparing usable kits; purchasing approval and spending rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Reconcile equipment custody and investigate stock discrepancies.
reach.learn: Serial-number control, stock adjustments and cycle counting.

evidence.claim: Catalogue requests, stock checks and approval-based purchase orders are standard deterministic purchasing workflows.
Scanning can reduce issue-record entry, while physical handover and condition checks remain human.
Equipment custody records linked to workers are personal data subject to GDPR.

assumptions: The company has approved suppliers, catalogue items and purchasing approval limits.
The task includes related buyer and stores handoffs; time shares cover that whole process.
Receipt and invoice processing are connected procure-to-pay tasks outside this task.
Automatic purchase orders cannot exceed approved commercial terms.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates.
unknowns: Quality of stock counts, equipment identifiers and supplier catalogues.
Whether existing purchasing and operations modules support reservations and scanning.
Which purchases require additional technical or budget approval.
Whether named custody records introduce consultation requirements under national rules.
research_questions: How often could available stock satisfy requests currently sent for purchase?
Which request fields can come directly from the approved resource plan?
What share of issue-record errors could scanning prevent?
new_work: Maintain catalogues, reorder settings and approval limits.
Resolve stock mismatches and failed purchase-order transmissions.
Handle substitutions, damaged equipment and overdue returns.
Maintain scanners, equipment identifiers and custody-record access.

More of the week goes to live recovery, customer agreements and safe coordination; dispatch authority remains human, and broader decision rights require explicit delegation.

Facilities manager: prioritize urgent service restoration across sites.
Business continuity planner: establish reliable field communication during outages.

role_batches.altitude: The dispatcher spends less of the week entering records, scanning screens and assembling recovery paperwork. More time goes to clarifying requests, negotiating repairs and approving workable schedule changes; decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Project management specialist: improve request readiness and scope definition.
Shipping, receiving and inventory clerk: reconcile job-level parts movements.

Logistics analyst: investigate recurring capacity bottlenecks.

Translate dispatch constraints into testable rules.
Read exception queues and assess data freshness.
Understand employee-data access and consultation requirements.

role_batches.altitude: The dispatcher moves from repeated lookup, copying and chasing toward resolving shortages, hazards and conflicting priorities. Existing assignment and escalation authority remains; wider staffing or spending rights need explicit delegation.
reach: Logistics analyst: forecast near-term capacity shortages.
Business continuity planner: prepare disruption and diversion plans.
Management analyst: diagnose recurring communication delays.

Assess data freshness and recognise infeasible plans.
Review extracted requirements against source documents.
